attribution.note: Marcus's own sentence in his Substack post, in his own voice.

semantics.note: The firm part, 'not profitable yet', is a present-tense observation. The hedged 'may never be' is rightly left out and is not scored.

contract.note: 'AI' is undefined. In context (isaiprofitable.com, labs' IPOs), reading it as the leading generative-AI labs and leaving out chip sellers is an ordinary, fair reading. Using net income as the main measure is reasonable.

evidence.note: OpenAI Q1 2026: net loss over $21B and operating loss of about $9.3B, per reporting on shareholder documents.
Anthropic H1 2026 net loss over $80B per WSJ/Reuters, published before the evaluation date. Mostly non-cash charges, but still a loss.

S-1 report: H1 net loss of $80.7B and H1 operating loss of $693M. Q2 operating income of $974M is a partial counterpoint, but it is not net profit for the period, so it does not meet the contradiction condition.

reviews.rationale: Both leading labs reported net losses for early to mid 2026. OpenAI had a Q1 net loss and operating loss; Anthropic had an H1 net loss and an H1 operating loss. Anthropic's Q2 operating profit is a nuance, not net profit across the sector. Under the contract's net-income measure, the claim holds.

attribution.note: Marcus states in his own words that costs are rising fast, adopting the Efrati report he quotes.

semantics.note: Faithful to the statement together with the tweet it introduces: the cost of developing Stargate and other AI data centers was rising fast.

contract.note: 'Rapidly' has no threshold. Taking double-digit per-GW rises or multi-fold component price rises as rapid is an ordinary plain reading, and the evidence clears it comfortably.

evidence.note: Bernstein, dated June 8 2026: per-GW AI data center capex about 17% above the Blackwell cycle. A translated secondary summary whose dollar figures look off by 10x, but the percentage is internally consistent.
Same Bernstein summary: NAND up about 115% a year to May 2026, with memory and storage pushing rack costs above earlier estimates.
Malaysia data centre construction costs up 9.3% a year, per Cushman & Wakefield. Regional and building-only, so context.
Server prices doubled from late 2023 to late 2025 and memory rose fivefold, per Bloomberg Intelligence. Mostly before the period, so context only.

reviews.rationale: Credible analyst estimates from around June 2026 show per-GW AI data center capex up about 17% generation over generation, driven by sharply rising memory and storage prices. No evidence shows flat or falling costs. Stargate-specific figures are unconfirmed, but the claim also covers other AI data centers.

attribution.note: Marcus's own sentence, stated with certainty.

semantics.note: 'Certainly ... will never' is an unhedged forecast with no deadline. The normalised version keeps the comparison to Amazon's IPO return.

contract.note: Defining 'comparable' as thousands of times the split-adjusted IPO price matches the post's 2,538x reference. Contradiction only, with no early confirmation, is fair for a 'never' claim.

evidence.note: Shows the June 2026 IPO at $135 and a first-day close about 19% up. This sets the baseline but does not resolve the forecast.

reviews.rationale: A 'never' forecast with no deadline. No conclusive event has occurred: SpaceX's return is nowhere near Amazon-like multiples. A shortfall so far does not confirm 'never', so the claim stays open.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words. The 2,538x figure comes from someone on X, but Marcus adopts it and makes the forecast himself.

semantics.note: 'Absolutely not going to happen' is a firm forecast that SpaceX will not match Amazon's 2,538x return (about $4,442T market cap). There is no deadline.

contract.note: Measuring from the split-adjusted IPO price is a reasonable baseline. The post's $4,442T base is unclear, but either baseline is far out of reach. Contradiction only is fair.

evidence.note: Shows the IPO baseline (offer at $135, roughly $2T value, first-day close about 19% up). It does not resolve the forecast.

reviews.rationale: An open-ended forecast. No event has reached the 2,538x threshold, and none can confirm 'never' early. The claim stays open.
